claims.text: Y2O3 is a high-melting, stable oxide suitable for dispersion in CoCrFeNi.
Dispersing nanoscale Y2O3 in CoCrFeNi will promote in-situ formation of a continuous, lubricious oxide tribolayer during sliding.
The Y2O3-modified alloy will maintain low friction and wear from approximately 25 °C to 800 °C.
A low volume fraction of nanoscale Y2O3 can be incorporated uniformly into the CoCrFeNi matrix.
Dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles will act as nucleation sites for rapid formation of a stable and continuous oxide tribolayer.
At low temperatures, Y2O3 nanoparticles will pin grain boundaries.
At low temperatures, Y2O3 nanoparticles will limit dislocation motion.
At high temperatures, Y2O3 nanoparticles will promote growth of a lubricious, protective oxide film.
The high-temperature oxide film will mitigate adhesive wear.
The oxide particles will retain microstructural stability at lower temperatures.
Impeded dislocation movement and grain-boundary sliding will reduce low-temperature wear.
At elevated temperatures, the particles will enable formation of a coherent, self-healing oxide film.
The coherent, self-healing oxide film will act as a solid lubricant and reduce friction and wear.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi exhibits increased friction and wear at elevated temperatures because of severe oxidation and microstructural softening.
Relative to unmodified CoCrFeNi, Y2O3-dispersed CoCrFeNi will have a lower and more stable coefficient of friction throughout approximately 25–800 °C.
Relative to unmodified CoCrFeNi, Y2O3-dispersed CoCrFeNi will have a lower wear rate throughout approximately 25–800 °C.
An excessively high oxide-particle volume fraction could embrittle the alloy.
Corrosive atmospheres could alter the proposed oxide-film formation mechanism.
